audit.whatIsWrong: win[4]/phases[4].side read Akshan, but whys[4] ('your Fate Sealed all-in outclasses his Comeuppance'), spikes[1] and late all claimed you win level 6 — the page answered its own level-6 row two ways. The packet also flags the chart as too Yone-favoured against a 47.37% win rate.
audit.why: Comeuppance is a 2500-range stored-bullet hit that scales with missing health; at 6 the ranged threat is his, not yours. Keeping the row as Akshan matches the win rate; the prose had to move to it, not the other way round.
audit.corrected: Chart sides left untouched (already Akshan at 6); whys[4], spikes[1] and late rewritten so the reasoning agrees with the row.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers anywhere, and the level-6 spike described Comeuppance as needing 'a marked scoundrel to matter in a duel' — Riot's text has no such condition on the ultimate. The Scoundrel mark belongs to Going Rogue (W).
audit.why: Comeuppance locks onto any enemy champion and fires stored bullets at the first champion, minion or structure hit. It threatens you in lane with no mark involved.
audit.corrected: Heroic Swing's 18s rank-1 cooldown added; the ult described accurately, including the fact that a minion in the line eats it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three things. (a) 'no sustain' / 'sustain-less' / 'resource-less marksman' — Dirty Fighting shields him every third hit from attacks and abilities, so short pokes are absorbed. (b) The page never states that Heroic Swing anchors to TERRAIN, so away from a wall he cannot cast it at all, and that colliding with a champion knocks him off mid-swing. (c) Going Rogue camouflage is never mentioned and you have no reveal in kit.
audit.why: These are the three levers that decide the lane: where you fight (terrain), how you end his escape (collision), and whether you can see him (vision).
audit.corrected: All three written into mid, spikes[2], breakdown.cooldowns and the do's.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing told the player to buy vision against a camouflage champion.
audit.why: Going Rogue drops to a 2s cooldown at rank 5 with 5500 range; without a Control Ward or sweeper you cannot track his roams.

edits.before: At 6 your Fate Sealed all-in outclasses his Comeuppance.
edits.after: At 6 Comeuppance snipes you out of your Fate Sealed window.

edits.before: First item you shred a sustain-less squishy marksman.
edits.after: First item you shred him past the Dirty Fighting shield.

edits.before: Your R (Fate Sealed) is a far stronger lane ult than his R (Comeuppance), which needs a marked scoundrel to matter in a duel. At 6 you out-all-in him — engage with Q3 knock-up into R when his E swing is on cooldown.
edits.after: Comeuppance stores bullets and hits the first champion, minion or structure in the line — at 6 he chunks you from 2500 range, so stand behind your wave and let a minion eat it. Hold Fate Sealed for his Heroic Swing.

edits.before: You keep the lead through first item: Akshan is a squishy marksman with no sustain, so your W shield and mixed DPS shred him in any extended trade. Deny his E resets by killing minions/vision he'd swing off.
edits.after: You can take first item: Akshan is squishy, and though Dirty Fighting shields him every third hit, your Spirit Cleave and mixed DPS out-last it in a long trade. Fight away from walls so Heroic Swing has nothing to anchor to.

edits.before: From level 2 onward this becomes even and then tilts your way: your Q dashes and W let you cross his poke range, and his E (Heroic Swing) travels on a fixed arc you can punish with a Q3 knock-up if he swings at you. He has no sustain and a squishy frame, so any trade you actually land hurts him more than his boomerang hurts you. By levels 4-5 you're the one dictating trades.
edits.after: From level 2 this evens out: your Q dashes and W cross his poke range, and Heroic Swing has to anchor to terrain — in the open middle of the lane he cannot swing at all. Colliding with a champion knocks him off it, so a Q3 knock-up into his arc ends the swing early. He is squishy, but Dirty Fighting shields him every third hit, so short pokes do less than you think.

edits.before: At 6 and beyond you're clearly ahead — your Fate Sealed is a real dueling ultimate while his Comeuppance needs a marked target to threaten you. Through first item and into the late game your durability, W shield, and mixed DPS beat a resource-less marksman in any extended fight, so force duels and use E to stick when he tries to swing away.
edits.after: At 6 the ranged threat is his: Comeuppance chunks you from 2500 range while Fate Sealed needs him in front of you. Through first item and beyond your durability, Spirit Cleave's shield and mixed DPS beat him in any extended fight, so force the duel on open ground where Heroic Swing has no wall, and use Soul Unbound to stick when he swings away.

edits.before: - Akshan Heroic Swing: matchup-defining — His dash + camera swing escape. Engage when it's down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Heroic Swing: 18s at rank 1, and it must anchor to terrain — away from walls he has no escape at all. - Going Rogue: he goes unseen, so a Control Ward and a sweeper are mandatory here. - Comeuppance: it stops on the first minion in the line.

edits.before: His dash + camera swing escape. Engage when it's down. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: It anchors to terrain, and any champion collision knocks him off it — Q3 into his arc.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Soul Unbound returns you to your body, not to safety — snap back early.

notes: The 'no sustain / sustain-less / resource-less marksman' framing appeared three times and is wrong: Dirty Fighting shields him every third hit. spikes[1] also invented a condition on Comeuppance (needing a marked Scoundrel) that belongs to Going Rogue. Level-chart sides were left alone — the packet flags the chart as too Yone-favoured for a 47.37% win rate, and the level-6 row already reads Akshan; I moved the contradicting prose onto that row instead of flipping more rows blind, since the akshan__yone mirror is already audited and its chart was not in mirrorFindings.
